metaDescription: Six brushless cordless string trimmers compared on RPM, swath, battery size and feed system, so you know what the brushless label really buys you in the yard.
expertTake: The Greenworks 60V 16 inch is the best brushless trimmer for rough ground and the Makita XRU23Z is the best choice for owners of 18V LXT packs. The Worx WG173 is the value pick for small lawns. Anyone with a flat suburban lawn does not need brushless and should save the difference.
introParagraphs: Brushless has become the headline word on string trimmer boxes, but it describes how a motor is switched, not how well a trimmer cuts. Electronic commutation removes the carbon brushes that wear out, runs cooler and wastes less battery as heat.

What you feel in the yard is steadier line speed under load and longer pack life, provided the rest of the machine keeps up. This guide checks six brushless models for swath, speed range, feed system and battery to see where the label pays off.

products.name: Greenworks 60V 16 in. Brushless String Trimmer, 2.5Ah, 6,000 RPM
products.description:
This is the brushless trimmer for the job that makes people buy gas. A 16 inch dual-line head with 0.095 inch line is one of the heaviest setups in battery trimming, and the maker says the motor matches a 26cc gas trimmer and can take on 1 inch vines. Speed is listed up to 6,000 RPM, but it is the torque from the 60V system under load that matters.

The reload system is the second thing to notice. A twist-on head lets you refill line in about ten seconds with no manual winding, which the maker contrasts with a bump feed head, and a bump feed on a dual-line 0.095 inch head is a chore. Fast reloading is what makes a heavy line usable on a large property.

The cost is weight and platform: a 16 inch head and a 60V pack are heavier than any 20V tool here, and the battery fits only the 60V line. A 2.5Ah pack is modest, so a large property wants a spare. Clear grass from the head after use and store the battery indoors. A twist-reload head is also a good fit for people who find the line-winding on conventional spools fiddly, since the work is done in seconds at the edge of the lawn. On a property with ditches, buy a second pack first and a spare spool second.
products.bestFor: Overgrown ditches, fence lines and rough ground.
cons: 2.5Ah pack runs flat on big jobs

products.name: Makita XRU23Z 18V LXT Brushless 13 in. String Trimmer, Tool Only
products.description:
Makita builds a brushless motor rated up to 6,000 RPM into a 13 inch trimmer on the 18V LXT platform. The maker claims up to an hour of runtime on a 4.0Ah battery, which, read as a best case, is a realistic figure for a 13 inch swath.

The tool is sold bare, so it suits those who already own LXT packs from other Makita tools. That is where the platform pays off: a drill, blower and trimmer can share two batteries. For someone starting from scratch, a battery and charger add to the cost, and the kit version of this trimmer is the more sensible entry.

The listing also points to the low-maintenance side of brushless: no gas, no oil mixing, no pull cord and low noise. It is a quiet, simple tool for a mid-sized lawn rather than a brush cutter. Check line length before each session and clear grass from the head. If you want more runtime, the maker's higher-capacity packs fit the same tool, and the savings from sharing packs across a drill and blower are real. Treat the one-hour claim as a ceiling for light grass, and expect closer to half in tall, wet growth.
products.bestFor: Mid-sized lawns for owners of Makita 18V LXT batteries.
pros: Up to 1 hour of runtime on 4.0Ah claimed
Runs on the wide LXT battery family
Low noise with no fuel or pull start

products.name: Worx WG173 20V 13 in. Brushless 3-in-1 String Trimmer, Edger and Mini Mower
products.description:
The WG173 is the low-cost way to get a brushless motor, and it does more than trim. A 90 degree pivot head turns it into an edger, and a wheeled deck converts it into a mini mower, which is useful for small banks and slopes. Electronic Command Feed advances line at the push of a button, so there is no bumping.

The maker claims a 4.0Ah battery and a high-torque brushless motor give gas-like power, which should be read as a claim for light and medium growth, not for thick brush. A 20V pack is the weak point on a tool with a motor of this size, so expect shorter runs on high-density grass than the 60V models provide.

It is the one to buy for a small or medium lawn where versatility matters and a 16 inch swath would be overkill. Clean the pivot and the wheel area after use and keep the battery away from cold sheds. Be realistic about the mini mower mode: it handles light turf on a bank, not thick lawn, and the plastic wheels will not like stones. Used as intended, the three modes mean one machine replaces a trimmer and an edger, which saves storage space as well.
products.bestFor: Small lawns that need trimming, edging and slope work.
pros: 3-in-1 with edger and mini mower modes

products.name: DCA 20V 14 in. Brushless 3-in-1 String Trimmer, 4000mAh, 2-Speed
products.description:
Two speeds make this brushless trimmer easy to match to the job. The low setting runs at 4,600 RPM for light trimming and edging and the high setting at 6,200 RPM for thick weeds, and the maker's runtime claim of 60 minutes on low and 36 on high shows what that choice costs.

The brushless motor is claimed to give 80 percent more stable power output, which is a way of saying the speed holds as the battery drains rather than fading. Auto feed handles the line, and a 14 inch swath is a bit wider than most 20V tools.

It is a smaller brand, so check parts and warranty before buying. The runtime figures are useful in that they are stated for both speeds, and they are a better guide than a single number. Use the low speed for most of the lawn and switch up only for the tough patches. That habit stretches the 4000mAh pack toward the 60 minute figure instead of the 36 minute one. When you buy a tool from a small brand, record the order date and keep the packaging, since warranty claims go more smoothly with proof.
products.bestFor: Mixed lawns where you switch between light and heavy growth.

products.name: Litheli 2x20V 14 in. Brushless String Trimmer, U20 Series, 2.5Ah

specList.label: Area claim
specList.value: Up to 1,076 sq ft per charge

products.description:
This trimmer ties two 20V batteries together for more output, which is a common way to get 40V-class power from a 20V platform. A 14 inch swath, two speeds at 5,000 and 6,000 RPM and a brushless motor make a solid mid-range tool.

The listing gives a coverage figure: about 1,076 square feet per charge, roughly the size of 16 parked cars. It is an unusual way to state runtime and a more useful one than minutes, since it ties battery life to area. A lawn of that size is a small yard, so the larger the lawn, the more charges you need.

It uses two packs per session, so you need to own or buy a second battery. Clear grass from the head and keep both packs charged to half before winter storage. Because two packs discharge together, a weak pack in the pair can cut a session short even if the other is full, so keep them as a matched set. Charge them together and use them together.
products.bestFor: Small to medium lawns where area-per-charge is the planning figure.
pros: Runtime stated as area per charge

products.name: Greenworks 80V 16 in. Brushless String Trimmer, 2.0Ah, 0.080 in. Dual Line
products.description:
The 80V version carries the same 16 inch swath as the 60V model but with a lighter 0.080 inch dual line and a bump feed head. Bump feed is simple and reliable, but it means tapping the head on the ground to advance line, which wears the head and wastes line on hard surfaces.

What the 80V platform gives you is a bigger battery family: the same pack runs the brand's mowers and blowers, so a household that owns those tools can add a trimmer without buying another battery. The 2.0Ah pack in the kit is small for a 16 inch head, so budget for a larger one.

It makes sense mainly for 80V owners. For others, the 60V model offers a heavier line and faster reload. Clear grass from the head and keep the line short enough not to overload the motor. If you do not already own 80V tools, the 60V model is the better first buy, because it brings a heavier line and a faster reload. If you do own them, it is the cheapest route to a 16 inch trimmer.
products.bestFor: Owners of Greenworks 80V mowers and blowers.
pros: Bump feed is simple to service
cons: 2.0Ah pack is small for this head
Bump feed wastes line on hard ground

buyingCriteria.explanation: A brushless motor uses electronics instead of carbon brushes, so it runs cooler and wastes less energy. For a lawn trimmed weekly the gain is mostly longer battery life and fewer repairs. For rough ground it holds line speed under load, as the Greenworks 60V does. Buyers often pay extra for the word and then use the tool on a lawn that a brushed unit would have handled, so be honest about your yard.

The Greenworks models cut 16 inches, the DCA and Litheli 14 and the Makita and Worx 13. Wider swaths cover ground faster but need more torque. Line thickness matters too, from 0.080 inch to 0.095 inch.

Two-speed trimmers like the DCA at 4,600 and 6,200 RPM and the Litheli at 5,000 and 6,000 RPM let you save charge on light growth. A single speed wastes battery on easy grass. Read RPM as a no-load figure.
The Worx has 4.0Ah, the DCA 4000mAh, the Greenworks 60V 2.5Ah and the 80V 2.0Ah. Platforms differ: LXT, 20V, 60V and 80V do not mix. Pick the pack you can live with.
Push-button and auto feed, as on the Worx and DCA, remove bumping. The Greenworks 60V reloads in about ten seconds. Bump feed on the 80V is simple but needs taps.
The 60V and 80V Greenworks tools are heavier. The 20V models are lighter. Over a half hour, weight matters more than a spec number, so match the tool to your stamina.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting capability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared swath, line size and speed. The Greenworks 60V with 0.095 inch line led for heavy growth.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pack size and stated runtimes. The DCA and Makita published runtimes, which counted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Feed and convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at line feed and modes. Push-button and fast reload scored highest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform value
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how widely each battery is used. Makita LXT and Greenworks platforms scored well. A tool on a small platform lost points even when its specs were good, since the battery is a long-term cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared sizes and styles. Lighter 20V tools scored well for comfort.

cards.label: Push-button or auto
cards.text: The Worx WG173 and DCA advance line without bumping. They waste less line on hard ground and are easier on the head.

cards.label: Bump or twist reload
cards.text: The Greenworks 80V uses bump feed and the 60V uses a twist reload. They suit heavier line but need more handling.

howToChoose.note: Choose push-button for tidy lawns and heavy line for brush.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a wide swath, a large battery and a fast line reload. A second battery matters more than any spec, because a lawn that takes more than one pack to finish is the commonest reason owners regret a purchase. Count the packs per mow before you pick a tool.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 60V 16 in. gives the widest swath and heaviest line. The Makita XRU23Z offers a claimed hour on 4.0Ah.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you cut heavy growth. The Greenworks 60V is the one to buy.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if your lawn is small. The Worx WG173 gives brushless power at a lower tier.

maintenance.why: Packed grass strains the motor and the bearing. Clear it with the battery removed. A brushless motor hides strain well, so do not wait for a sound change before you check.

Short line cuts a smaller swath. Fit fresh line to the correct length. Use line of the diameter the head is rated for, because oversize line overloads the motor and can overheat a brushless controller.
Cold lowers capacity and a pack left flat for months can fail to recharge at all. Keep at half charge in a dry, frost-free room.
A bent guard lets line wrap around the head and stalls the motor. Straighten or replace it, and check the shaft coupling for play at the same time.
Grit makes the head stiff on 3-in-1 models and stops it locking in position. Brush it clean and add a drop of light oil to the pivot pin once a year.

faq.a: For frequent use and heavy growth, yes. It runs cooler and wastes less energy. For a small lawn, a brushed trimmer is cheaper. The benefit shows up over years of ownership, because there are no brushes to replace and the motor runs cooler.
It is a marketing comparison to an engine size. Use it as a rough guide, and compare swath, line and battery instead.

faq.q: How long will a battery last?
faq.a: Makita claims up to 1 hour on 4.0Ah and the DCA 60 minutes on low. Heavy growth cuts that. Cold weather and old packs cut it further, so use the claimed figure only as a way to compare models.

faq.q: Do I need a spare battery?
faq.a: For larger lawns, yes. A 2.0Ah pack on a 16 inch head will run flat quickly.
Check the head's rated line size. The Greenworks 60V takes 0.095 inch and the 80V 0.080 inch.
Only within a platform. LXT, 20V, 60V and 80V packs do not fit each other.
